topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by outlining its main learning outcomes and connecting the content to prior practical histopathology sessions.

topics.label: Discovery of proto-oncogenes through tumor virology and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the historical study of tumor viruses and cell transformation assays established that cancer originates from altered normal cellular genes.

topics.label: Functional classification and genetics of oncogenes and tumor suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer-promoting mutations are categorized and function, focusing on the genetic mechanisms that distinguish oncogenes from tumor suppressors.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of genomic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the causes and cellular effects of genomic instability, showing how defects in DNA repair and chromosome segregation alter the genome.

topics.label: Multistep tumor progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how the stepwise accumulation of somatic and inherited genetic alterations drives tumor progression and influences clinical outcomes.

topics.label: Conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the lecturer's concluding remarks, invites student questions, and suggests supplementary reading.
